evidence: Cic. Har. Resp. 15: annō superiōre (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. last year: superiōre annō
Traupman 89: the previous year, superior annus
terms.comment: annō superiōre, last year; superiōribus diēbus, in the previous days (Caes. BG 7.58, Lewis & Short); superiōre hebdomade, last week (see last week). Of nights, though, proximā nocte is last night and superiōre nocte the night before (Cic. Cat. 1.1).

evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.1: quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs
terms.comment: It means either the last or the next; the tense tells which (see last night, next week).

evidence: Caes. BG 3.29: cīvitātēs quae proximē bellum fēcerant (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 3.9.7: priōre annō, the year before (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The earlier of two, set against posterior; Cicero keeps superior for earlier in general, when no other time is named (Lewis & Short). Its neuter prius is the adverb before (see previously).

phrases.latin: quid proximā, quid superiōre nocte ēgerīs
phrases.english: what you did last night, and what the night before
Last year we were in Portugal.
